diagnostic_evidence.quote: The union of the disjoint sets $L_{\bsl(u,\bsk')}$ over all $\bsk' \le \bsk$ covers exactly the set of all Walsh indices $\bsh$ where $h_j < b^{k_j+1}$ for all $j \in u$ and $h_j=0$ for $j \notin u$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of Lemma 4.1 relies directly on identity (14), which claims that the sum of ANOVA components $\beta_{u,\bsk'}$ over all $\bsk' \le \bsk$ equals $\tilde{\beta}_{u,u,\bsk}$. This identity is false in general: whenever $f_\emptyset = \int_{[0,1)^d} f(\bsx)d\bsx \neq 0$, the integral of the left-hand side over $[0,1)^{|u|}$ is 0 by orthogonality, whereas the integral of the right-hand side is $f_\emptyset$. In Appendix A, the argument purporting to prove (14) falsely states that the disjoint sets $L_{\bsl(u,\bsk')}$ cover all Walsh indices with $h_j < b^{k_j+1}$ for $j \in u$; in fact, $L_{\bsl}$ requires $h_j \ge b^{l_j-1} \ge 1$ for all $j \in u$, completely omitting all Walsh indices where $h_j = 0$ for any $j \in u$. The true relation is $\tilde{\beta}_{u,u,\bsk}(\bsx_u) = f_\emptyset + \sum_{\emptyset \neq w \subseteq u} \sum_{\bsk'_w \le \bsk_w} \beta_{w,\bsk'_w}(\bsx_w)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace identity (14) with the full decomposition $\tilde{\beta}_{u,u,\bsk}(\bsx_u) = f_\emptyset + \sum_{\emptyset \neq w \subseteq u} \sum_{\bsk'_w \le \bsk_w} \beta_{w,\bsk'_w}(\bsx_w)$, and update the proof of Lemma 4.1 to note that the components for all proper subsets $w \subsetneq u$ vanish under the alternating sum $\sum_{v \subseteq u} (-1)^{|u|-|v|}$.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Lemma 4.1 is mathematically invalid as written. However, the statement of Lemma 4.1 is true, so no downstream results are invalidated once the proof is repaired.
issues.title: Invalid ANOVA identity and defective proof of Lemma 4.1
issues.why_classification: A short, routine local repair to the proof of Lemma 4.1 and Appendix A fully restores the result, leaving every substantive claim and rate in the paper intact.
